items.question: What is $y$ when $x = -4$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide 6 by −4, keeping the sign.

items.question: What is the lowest value $f$ takes?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The lowest point is halfway between the roots. Find its height.

byKey.x: 4 is where the lowest point is, its $x$. The lowest value is the height there, $f(4)$.

explain.text: A U is a mirror image about its turning point, so the turning point is halfway between the roots, at $x = 4$. The lowest value is $f(4) = -4$.

items.question: Drag the seven points to sketch it from $x = -3$ to $x = 3$.

items.question: Above £100.00, at what expiry price does it make a profit of £5.00?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find where the P&L graph reaches height 5.

byKey.no-premium: You forgot the £8.00 you paid. The rise must first earn that back, then £5.00 more.
byKey.breakeven: £108.00 is where P&L is 0. We want the price where it is 5.

explain.text: We solve P&L = 5: the line at height 5 meets the right arm of the V. The call gains £1.00 per £1.00 above £100.00, so it needs a rise of $8 + 5 = 13$: £113.00.

Draw the line $y = x + 6$ on the graph of $y = x^3$
Read the only crossing, where both sides are equal: $(2, 8)$

feedback.correct: Rearrange, draw, read, keep the $x$-value, check.

items.prose: A car has gone $d = t^2$ metres after $t$ seconds. Over the first 4 seconds its average speed is $16 \div 4 = 4$ m/s. The touching line at P shows the gradient.
items.question: Drag P to the moment when the car's speed equals that average.

feedback.correct: At $t = 2$ the gradient is 4 m/s, equal to the average.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find where the touching line's gradient reads 4.

byKey.end: At $t = 4$ the car is doing 8 m/s, double the average. The average is matched earlier.

explain.text: The speed is the gradient, $2t$ here, and it equals 4 when $t = 2$. Halfway through the 4 seconds, the car is going at exactly its average speed.

items.title: A bond price curve
items.prompt: A zero-coupon bond pays £100.00 in 5 years. At yield $y$ (as a decimal) its price is $P(y) = \dfrac{100}{(1 + y)^5}$ pounds. (a) Make a table of prices at yields of 0%, 2%, 4% and 6%, to two decimal places. (b) Describe the shape of the graph of price against yield, and say what the gradient means, with units. (c) Compare the fall in price from 0% to 2% with the fall from 4% to 6%, and say what that tells you about the curve. (d) Use your table to estimate the yield at which the price is £80.00, and check your estimate.
items.model:
**(a) Table.**

| Yield | $(1 + y)^5$ | Price |
|---|---|---|
| 0% | 1 | £100.00 |
| 2% | 1.10408 | £90.57 |
| 4% | 1.21665 | £82.19 |
| 6% | 1.33823 | £74.73 |

Each price is 100 divided by $(1 + y)^5$, for example $100 \div 1.21665 = 82.19$.

**(b) Shape.** The price falls as the yield rises, so the curve is decreasing. It bends upwards: it is convex, flattening as the yield grows, like the right-hand piece of $y = \tfrac{1}{x}$. It never reaches 0, because $\tfrac{100}{(1 + y)^5}$ is positive for every yield. The gradient is the change in price per change in yield, in pounds per percentage point. It is negative everywhere.

**(c) Falls.** From 0% to 2% the price falls $100.00 - 90.57 = £9.43$. From 4% to 6% it falls $82.19 - 74.73 = £7.46$. The same 2-point rise in yield costs less each time, so the gradient is getting less negative: the curve is flattening, which is what convex means.

**(d) Estimate.** £80.00 lies between £82.19 (4%) and £74.73 (6%). It is $82.19 - 80.00 = 2.19$ of the $7.46$ drop, about 0.29 of the way, so the yield is about $4 + 0.29 \times 2 \approx 4.6\%$. Check: $1.046^5 \approx 1.252$ and $100 \div 1.252 \approx 79.86$, close to £80.00. The exact yield is about 4.56%. Reading between table points along a straight line slightly overestimates it, because the true curve sags below that line.

rubric.text: Computes all four prices correctly to two decimal places.
Describes the curve as decreasing and convex (flattening), never reaching 0.
States that the gradient is pounds per percentage point of yield, and that it is negative.
Finds the falls £9.43 and £7.46 and links the smaller fall to the curve flattening.
Estimates the yield for £80.00 between 4% and 6%, at about 4.6%.
Checks the estimate by substituting it back into the price rule.
